testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, the driver should:

options.text: Make sure the cargo weight does not exceed legal weight limits.
Open each container to check it.
Unseal the load to check safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the cargo weight does not exceed legal weight limits.
questions.explanation: Drivers cannot open sealed loads to inspect them. However, they must make sure the total weight and axle weight do not exceed legal limits.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, you should:

options.text: Use only your brakes to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: On a steep hill, use engine braking as your main way to control speed. Downshift before you start going downhill. If you rely too much on brakes, they can overheat and stop working.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that requires a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For your safety, you must wear your seat belt every time you operate a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When driving in heavy traffic, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not use your cell phone.
questions.explanation: Heavy traffic requires your full attention. Avoid all distractions, including any cell phone use, in these areas.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: To tell the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
To ensure vehicles are inspected regularly.
To hold drivers responsible for inspecting their vehicles.
To plan the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: To tell the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report lets the driver report safety issues to the motor carrier. Fill one out after each day of driving. Note any problems that could affect safe operation or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: When checking tire condition during a vehicle inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure the inside edges are more worn than the outside edges.
Make sure the outside edges are more worn than the inside edges.
Make sure the middle is more worn than the outside edges.
Make sure the tires wear evenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the tires wear evenly.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check that tire treads are worn evenly across the entire tire.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: The vehicle crosses over an exercise boundary line.
A driver does a single pull-up.
A driver puts the vehicle in neutral and applies the parking brake.
The vehicle stalls while shifting gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle crosses over an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment is when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during an exercise. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: Not draining the tanks in an air brake system can cause:

options.text: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much fuel to be carried.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water to freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks must be drained to remove water and oil that build up. If water is left in the system, it can freeze in cold weather and make brakes fail.

questions.question: Federal and state laws require drivers to:

options.text: Inspect their vehicles only if they think there might be a problem.
Inspect their vehicles only when traveling out-of-state.
Inspect their vehicles only if carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect their vehicles regularly.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers must inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections help find problems before they become dangerous or expensive.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver puts the vehicle in neutral and applies the parking brake.
The vehicle touches an exercise boundary line.
A driver completes an exercise correctly.
An applicant tries to bribe the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touches an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment is when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during an exercise. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: During the on-road driving skills test, you will be tested on how you use gears. Which should you NOT do?

options.text: Select a gear that does not rev the engine.
Forget to shift through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift while taking a turn.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, you will be tested on gear usage. Use a gear that does not rev or lug the engine. Avoid grinding and clashing gears. Do not shift while turning or going through intersections.

questions.question: When you approach your vehicle, you should check that:

options.text: The vehicle is shinier than other vehicles.
The vehicle is not parked too close to other vehicles.
There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
questions.explanation: Before you inspect your vehicle, check its condition. Make sure it is not damaged or leaning. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Also check around the vehicle for hazards, such as people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or tree limbs.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle without scraping ice off the windshield
The driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards on the road. Examples include: drivers with ice on windshields, drivers with large items blocking windows, and drivers of rental trucks who are not used to the truck's limited rear visibility.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, the coolant temperature gauge should:

options.text: Not change from where it starts.
Slowly rise to the normal operating range.
Jump quickly to the normal operating range.
Flash until it reaches the normal operating range.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly rise to the normal operating range.
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after you start the engine. The coolant temperature gauge should slowly rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a low air pressure warning light. The warning light is red and may also have a buzzer.

questions.question: To fix a drive-wheel braking skid, you should do all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Remove your foot from the brake pedal.
Turn quickly in the direction of the skid.
Turn back after the vehicle is back on course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: To fix a drive-wheel braking skid, first lift your foot off the brake pedal so the locked wheels can roll again. Quickly steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Then turn back to stop the vehicle from skidding in the opposite direction.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, so it looks like the road is just wet.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks need special care because:

options.text: They have low centers of gravity.
They have high centers of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and their loads often shift while the vehicle is moving. Be extra careful when turning and taking curves with this type of vehicle.

questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, you should:

options.text: Park in a busy area near trees.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in an open area.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop right away. Park in an open area away from anything that could catch fire, like plants or other vehicles. Do not pull into a gas station.

questions.question: Which of the following is a serious traffic violation?

options.text: Driving 15 mph or more above the posted speed limit
Traffic offenses in a CMV that cause personal injury accidents
Not stopping completely at a stop sign
Traveling in a group of more than five CMVs

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving 15 mph or more above the posted speed limit
questions.explanation: Serious traffic violations include: speeding 15 mph or more above the limit, reckless driving, improper or erratic lane changes, following too closely, traffic offenses in a CMV that cause fatal accidents, driving a CMV without a CDL or without it in your possession, and driving a CMV without the correct CDL class or endorsements.

questions.question: During the skills test, when you need to stop before making a turn, you should:

options.text: Stop after the stop line to see better.
Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead. Do not let your vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can still see its rear tires.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn frequently while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and sleep.
questions.explanation: Frequent yawning means you are tired. The only safe thing to do is stop and get sleep. Coffee and other stimulants will eventually wear off and make you even more tired.

questions.question: When driving on an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors to see traffic around you.
Stay on the left side of the lane.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors to see traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Keep your lane position correct and stay the right distance from other vehicles. Drive at the speed limit. Check all around you for traffic using your mirrors.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Keeps the load from moving around.
Can only be done in dry weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps the load from moving around.
questions.explanation: Blocking stops cargo from sliding during transport. If the load shifts, it makes the truck harder to steer and control.

questions.question: If you must back up, it helps to:

options.text: Back up fast to finish quickly.
Get out and walk around to check for hazards first.
Use only the passenger side mirror.
Stick your head out the window and look back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to check for hazards first.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk around the truck to look for obstacles in your path. Use both mirrors while backing up. Back up slowly.

questions.question: If you are convicted of breaking texting laws two or more times at the state level, your CDL may be:

options.text: Not affected if the violations happened in another state.
Not affected if you text quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Suspended for six months.
questions.explanation: If convicted of breaking texting laws two or more times, your CDL will be suspended. A second offense within three years results in 60 days suspension. A third or later offense within three years results in 120 days suspension.

questions.question: Before driving a truck with dual air brakes, air pressure of at least ____ must be built up in both brake systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Let the air compressor build up pressure to at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary brake systems before you drive.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo:
questions.correctAnswerText: Creates an unbalanced load.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat makes the load unbalanced. The truck may become top-heavy, and the swinging meat can make steering difficult. Be extra careful on sharp curves, like highway ramps.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should not:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: It is best not to drive in fog. If you must drive in fog, slow down. Use low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.question: When using road speed to decide when to shift gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as your guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Learn which speeds work for each gear by reading your vehicle's manual. Watch your speedometer and shift up when you reach the right speed for that gear.

questions.question: In very hot weather, tires should be checked regularly because:

options.text: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
The tread wears down extra quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands. This increases the air pressure in your tires. If this happens, stop and let your tires cool. Do not let air out. Letting air out will cause the pressure to drop too low when the tires cool.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks are used in an air brake system?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number varies.
questions.explanation: Different vehicles have different numbers of air storage tanks. The number and size depend on the vehicle.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, drivers must check the securement of the cargo every:
questions.correctAnswerText: 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before starting, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually occurs:

options.text: In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water builds up on the road. Low tire pressure or worn tire tread makes it more likely. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water.

questions.question: You may be denied a HazMat endorsement if:

options.text: You are a lawful resident of the United States.
You have renounced your United States citizenship.
You have only been convicted of misdemeanors.
You do not suffer from a mental illness.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have renounced your United States citizenship.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a HazMat endorsement if you are not a U.S. lawful permanent resident; you renounce U.S. citizenship; you are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies; you are judged mentally unstable; or you pose a security threat to the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: While driving, spring brakes are generally held in place by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you must wait for the air compressor to build a minimum of ____ in both the primary and secondary systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey all traffic signs and signals, but only if other traffic is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey all traffic signs and signals, but only if other traffic is present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road test. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and signals at all times, following all traffic laws, and completing the test with no accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: Drivers are usually the least alert:
questions.correctAnswerText: Late at night.
questions.explanation: Drivers are least alert when driving late at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: If you experience a loss of hydraulic pressure, you should do all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate.
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic pressure in your brakes, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Find an escape route, such as an escape ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Report the driver.
questions.explanation: Get out of the aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact or gesture at them. Once you are safe, report them to the police.

questions.question: How should you do a driver's side parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Pass the parking space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the parking space without passing it first.
Back into the parking space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back into it. Position your vehicle so it is completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing railroad tracks?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, shift gears, pass, or change lanes while crossing railroad tracks. Stay in your lane until you have completely cleared the tracks.

questions.question: What can cause hydraulic brakes to fail?

options.text: Driving uphill for long periods of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: A loss of pressure.
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes fail when hydraulic pressure is lost. Brakes can also fade from overuse on long downhill drives.

questions.question: How should weight be loaded into a trailer?

options.text: Placed only on the left side, if possible.
Placed only on the right side, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Placed as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load weight as low as possible in the trailer. Weight placed too high increases the risk of the vehicle tipping over.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery right after rain starts?

options.text: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
The gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road. This creates a slippery surface that is very dangerous.

questions.question: How can you increase visibility at dawn or dusk?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turning on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating located?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a specific pressure. This information is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: What are passive railroad crossings?

options.text: Are not controlled by any type of traffic control device.
Have gates that lower when trains are approaching.
Should never be crossed by a CMV.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not controlled by any type of traffic control device.
questions.explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control devices. Drivers must decide on their own whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you fall behind on sleep
When you want to take a nap
The amount of time it takes to get ready to drive after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: When you fall behind on sleep
questions.explanation: Sleep debt happens when you do not get enough sleep. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.
